question: A shopkeeper sold a book for ₹544 at a loss of 36%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell it to gain 24% on it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Prices** is equivalent to the ratio of (100 − **Loss%**) and (100 + **Gain%**).

Initial SP : New SP = (100 − 36) : (100 + 24) = 64 : 124.

Given: 64 units = ₹544 ⇒ 1 unit = 544 ÷ 64 = 8.5.

New SP = 124 × 8.5 = ₹1,054.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,054.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial SP = ₹544, Loss = 36%, Desired Gain = 24%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%), New SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2f391a602b5c3c989fd35d2518c40d76d0ee55343b3503e7495dd36b14d989c.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 544 × 100 ÷ (100 − 36) = 544 × 100 ÷ 64 = ₹850.

⇒ **New Selling Price** = 850 × (100 + 24) ÷ 100 = 850 × 124 ÷ 100.

⇒ **New Selling Price** = 8.5 × 124 = ₹1,054.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,054.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation of SP and Percentage

When CP is constant, SP₁ ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss₁) = SP₂ ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss₂).

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **Selling Price** > **Cost Price**, while Loss occurs when **Cost Price** > **Selling Price**.
